land.text: the Sous valley around Iligh, escaping the weakened Saadian makhzen under Sultan Zaydan

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by the Saadians'; the Saadi dossier records the Sous loss in 1614 and the Draa valley in 1631.

land.text: the Sous and the Draa valley: 'In 1670, the Alaouites razed Iligh, bringing a definitive end to Tazerwalt's political independence'

successors.note: The Kingdom of Tazeroualt page gives 1681 (Mawlay al-Rashid destroying the fortress); the Alawi dossier has al-Rashid reigning 1664-1672, so 1670 is used.

capitals.name: Iligh (Illigh)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Illigh'; 'After al-Hahi's death in 1626, Iligh became the capital of Sous'. The coordinates are approximate (the village is not in the gazetteer; Tiznit is 20 km away).

correction.text: the zawiya and its home district at Iligh in the Anti-Atlas (Tazerwalt)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'He was a great-grandson of Sidi Ahmed Ou Moussa, founder of the Zawiya of Illigh, and became its head in 1613'; the page gives no area. A 40 km circle around Tiznit stands for the home district.

correction.text: the Sous valley led from Iligh since 1614

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'After Ahmed ibn Abi Mahalli was defeated in 1614, Abu Hassun mobilized the Sous Berbers against the weakened Sultan Zaydan'; Iligh becomes 'the capital of Sous' after 1626. The shape is the Sous region without the Draa circle, as the Saadi dossier draws its 1614 loss.

correction.text: the Sous, the Draa valley and Sijilmasa in the Tafilalt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'He seized Sijilmasa in 1631 and held it until the Alawis expelled him in 1640. He also expanded into the Draa valley.' The Draa radius is the Saadi dossier's (110 km around 30.4 N 6 W); the Tazerwalt page adds Touat and Taghaza as trade-route holdings, which are not drawn.

correction.text: the Sous and the Draa valley, after the loss of Sijilmasa

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Tazerwalt page says the Alaouites of the Tafilalt captured Sijilmasa 'in the late 1650s' and that Sidi Ali Bou Dmia died in 1659; the Kingdom page has the expulsion in 1640, which the ledger follows.

region.text: the zawiya and its district at Iligh

ledger.note: 1613: Ali Abu Hassun heads the Zawiya of Iligh. Infobox 'Established: 1613'; he 'became its head in 1613', a great-grandson of Sidi Ahmed Ou Moussa; the Tazerwalt page begins the amirate after Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur's death in 1603.

region.text: the Sous valley led from Iligh

ledger.note: 1614: Abu Hassun rallies the Sous against the Saadis. 'After Ahmed ibn Abi Mahalli was defeated in 1614, Abu Hassun mobilized the Sous Berbers against the weakened Sultan Zaydan'; Iligh is the capital of Sous after 1626. The extent is the Saadi dossier's reading of the Sous.

region.text: the Draa valley, a 110 km circle around 30.4 N 6 W

ledger.note: 1631: the Draa valley joins. 'He also expanded into the Draa valley' (undated on the page); 1631 is the year the page gives for Sijilmasa and the Saadi dossier's year for the Draa.

1631: Abu Hassun seizes Sijilmasa. 'He seized Sijilmasa in 1631 and held it until the Alawis expelled him in 1640.' The Alawi dossier has Mawlay al-Sharif declared sultan of the Tafilalt in the same year; the pages disagree on who held the town.
1640: the Alawis expel Abu Hassun from Sijilmasa. 'held it until the Alawis expelled him in 1640'; the Tazerwalt page instead has the Alaouites of Tafilalt capture Sijilmasa 'in the late 1650s'.

region.text: the Sous and the Draa, the Zawiya's principality

ledger.note: 1670: the Alaouites raze Iligh. 'In 1670, the Alaouites razed Iligh, bringing a definitive end to Tazerwalt's political independence.' The Kingdom of Tazeroualt page puts the end in 1681 (Mawlay al-Rashid destroying the fortress of Iligh) and a revival under Hashim ibn Ali (d. 1825) and Husayn (d. 1886).

wars.name: Mawlay al-Sharif against Abu Hassun
wars.outcome: 'Around 1635 or 1636, Mawlay al-Sharif unsuccessfully tried to drive out Abu Hassun's troops and was exiled to Sous'; his son Mawlay Ismail later became sultan.
wars.note: The page does not say where the attempt took place.

wars.name: Alawite conquest of Tazerwalt
wars.outcome: The Alawis expelled Abu Hassun from Sijilmasa in 1640; Sidi Ali Bou Dmia died in 1659 and was briefly succeeded by his son Muhammad; the Alaouites razed Iligh in 1670 and ended the principality's independence.
wars.note: The Kingdom of Tazeroualt page gives 1681 and Mawlay al-Rashid; the Tazerwalt page gives 1670 without a ruler.

wars.name: Zaydan's Saadi war against the Sous
wars.outcome: Abu Hassun mobilised the Sous Berbers against the weakened Sultan Zaydan after 1614; Iligh became the capital of Sous after al-Hahi's death in 1626. The page names no battle.

certainty.note: A maraboutic principality of the Anti-Atlas and the Draa: no page gives a frontier; the Draa circle is the Saadi dossier's.

notes: Cliopatria has no Illigh row. The sibling Saadi dossier (af-02-e) uses the slug zawiya-of-illigh for its 1614 (Sous) and 1631 (Draa) losses, which this dossier mirrors with the same region specs. Pages conflict: start 1613 (Kingdom page infobox) vs 1603 (Tazerwalt page: 'After Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur died in 1603, his grandson Sidi Ali Bou Dmia declared himself amir'); end 1681 (Kingdom page, with al-Rashid, who per the Alawi dossier reigned 1664-1672) vs 1670 (Tazerwalt page); the Kingdom page has Sijilmasa held 1631-1640 and the Tazerwalt page has the Alaouites take it in the late 1650s; the Tazerwalt page says the amirate 'by the mid-17th century' controlled Touat and Taghaza (not drawn). The House of Iligh regained 'significant political and military strength' and 'controlled much of the Souss region' in the 18th-19th centuries (Tazerwalt page; Hashim ibn Ali d. 1825, Husayn d. 1886, subdued by Hassan I in 1882 per the Kingdom page): that second life has no dates on the pages and is not entered; a gap-filler could extend this dossier. The Ali Abu Hassun article (Wattasid regent d. 1554) is a different person and was not used. Gazetteer: Sous, Tiznit and Sijilmasa resolve; Iligh is not a place there (needed: Iligh, Anti-Atlas, c. 29.8 N 9.5 W).
